title: The Periodic Table as a Measured Object II: A Nuclear-Informed Cross-Scale Sequel on What Sharpens, Collapses, and Inverts Under a Stronger Atomic Closure
object_of_study: changes in atomic structural distinctions under a strengthened nuclear-informed measurement surface
main_question: Which distinctions in the first atomic closure sharpen, collapse, or invert when nuclear information is added under a stronger frozen surface?

claim_layers.claim: The 12-channel closure yields a mixed but stronger readback: retention and coherence rise, heterogeneity and curvature rise, Collapse rows increase, Watch rows contract, Stable remains absent, the Critical overlay falls (Zenodo record description).
The library places this work as a domain translation extending the first periodic-table closure (REL-000003).

scope: Replacement of the 8-channel surface by a 12-channel closure admitting neutron excess, binding energy per nucleon, magic-number proximity, valence-electron structure, and block order; comparison of readbacks against the first closure.
exclusions: Does not claim the periodic table originates from the kernel.
Does not claim the strengthened closure is simply better.
preserved_meaning: The source's mixed readback: arithmetic retention and multiplicative coherence rise while heterogeneity and curvature also rise; Collapse rows increase, Watch contracts, Stable remains absent, Critical falls.

distortion_or_substitution_risk: Reading the stronger closure as a superior or final atomic account rather than a more revealing and more demanding comparison surface.
